Maya: Heads up — after yesterday's autotuner change I see a regression on short-seq (<64) p50/p95 for the 16k-token attention model on A100. Perf test: dev-infer-suite/seq-short. p95 went from 28ms -> 38ms.
Aaron: Can you paste the exact job id / command you ran? Also which kernel picker commit?
Maya: job=perf/2026-11-11/shot-73; kernel-picker rev=ab3f9d (autotune: choose smem-tiling when est-occupancy >= 0.6). Ran default microbench harness: `./run_microbench --model=16k-attn --seq=32 --bs=1 --arch=a100`
perf-bot: [alert] perf/regression detected job=perf/2026-11-11/shot-73 metric=p95 delta=+36% baseline=28ms current=38ms trace=ci/4372
Sasha: Curious. My quick nvprof shows a lot of spill stores when the smem-tiling path is chosen. Register usage jumped ~12 regs/function -> spilling, which kills occupancy and adds global stores. I can attach flame snippet.
Liam: That matches what I guessed — the new picker is favoring a tiled-smem kernel for short sequences on A100 because it estimated higher occupancy, but it didn't account for the per-block register pressure for this model config. For short seq the kernel's per-thread register live set *increases* because of simplified loop-unrolling, causing spills.
Aaron: Can you drop the nvprof output here? Also what tile_size was chosen? If tile_size is large it can increase register pressure.
Sasha: nvprof snippet (truncated):
```
== Profiler result ==
Kernel: tiled_smem_v2
Registers per thread: 64  <-- spilled (spill stores: 12345)
L1/global stores increased: +18%
Achieved occupancy: 0.52
```
Tile size picked: 128x8 (tile_x=128, tile_y=8).
Maya: Old autotune used tile 64x8 for this exact workload on A100 and we had regs=52 + occupancy 0.65. New rule bumped tile_x to 128 because throughput-estimator favored bigger tiles at longer seqs; but we didn't gate by per-arch reg budget.
Aaron: Repro plan: run the microbench sweep that tests tile_x in [32,64,96,128] and warp specialization on/off, and collect regs/spills and pX metrics. Command: `./microbench_sweep --model=16k-attn --seq=32 --arch=a100 --tile_x=32,64,96,128 --warp_split=auto,off --out=./sweep_out.json`
Liam: Also add an experiment that forces the alt kernel path (non-smem) for short seq to confirm regression is purely due to kernel switch. `--force_kernel=non_smem`
Sasha: Quick stat: when forced to non_smem kernel p95=26ms on same job. So it's definitely the tiled_smem path.
Maya: Hypothesis: autotuner's scoring function weights 'estimated arithmetic intensity' too high for seq<64 on A100 and doesn't account for register pressure. We should add an architecture-aware reg_budget estimate and prefer lower-register kernels when registers estimate > threshold (per-arch e.g., A100=60, H100=72).
Aaron: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: lower tile_x cap for A100 for seq<64, or add a per-kernel reg_penalty to score: score -= alpha * max(0, est_regs - arch_reg_budget). alpha tuned conservatively.
perf-bot: [info] recorded experiment -> sweep job id=exp/2026-11-11/sweep-9 config=tile-sweep+warp-split
Sasha: I can run the sweep now and upload logs. Expect run ~25m. Will post summarized table with p50/p95/regs/spills.
Maya: If sweep confirms, I'll land a small patch to the autotuner that adds reg_penalty + per-arch thresholds and a guard: avoid smem-tiling if est_spills>0 for seq<=64.
Liam: For longer-term, we should add a lightweight static estimator that computes expected register live set for a kernel given tile params and unroll factors. That can be used by the picker before launching expensive sample runs.
Aaron: Also watch KV cache path: if cache hit rates are low then sequence lengths vary and picker might flip mid-rollout. We need hysteresis: don't change kernel unless sustained throughput difference > X for N minutes.
Maya: Good point — we saw flips during the canary traffic spike. I'll add a rollout guard.
Sasha: Uploading sweep partial results: (summary)
- tile_x=32 warp_split=off => p95=30ms regs=50 spills=0 occ=0.68
- tile_x=64 warp_split=off => p95=28ms regs=52 spills=0 occ=0.65
- tile_x=96 warp_split=auto => p95=33ms regs=62 spills=8 occ=0.58
- tile_x=128 warp_split=auto => p95=38ms regs=64 spills=15 occ=0.52
Full logs: s3://perf-logs/exp/2026-11-11/sweep-9/*.log
Aaron: Nice data. That makes the decision easy. For seq<=64 on A100 we cap tile_x<=64. I'll prototype the scoring patch and Maya can run canary.
Maya: I'll schedule canary for this afternoon: route 5% of short-seq traffic to patched picker. Will watch p95 and KV hit behavior.
Liam: If canary looks good, we should also add a regression test in CI that runs the short-seq microbench on A100 and asserts p95 <= 1.1*baseline.
Maya: Agreed. Assigning: Aaron -> scoring patch PR, Sasha -> full sweep logs + nvprof artifacts, Maya -> canary + rollout guard, Liam -> add CI regression test. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Aaron: On it.
Sasha: Uploading nvprof tar to s3 and linking in the ticket.

Maya: Thanks team :thumbsup:
Aaron: :+1:
